explain.say: Imagine a time machine. You can zoom to yesterday, stay in today, or jump to tomorrow. Verbs have a time machine too, called tense. Look at the timeline on the board. The first stop is yesterday: I walked.

faq.a: The past tense tells you something already happened. Many verbs add ed, like walked and played; some change, like ate and went.
asks: What is the past tense of walk?

faq.a: The present tense tells you something happens now or happens often: I walk to school, or I am walking now.

faq.q: How do I write the future tense?
faq.a: Put will before the verb: I will walk, she will sing. You can also say going to: I am going to walk.
Past, present and future. Each one has extra forms too, like I was walking or I have walked.

faq.q: Why should a story stay in one tense?
faq.a: Jumping between tenses confuses the reader about when things happen. Most stories are told in the past tense from start to end.
asks: Can I change tense in a story?

facts: Mandarin Chinese verbs do not change form for tense; time words and small particles show when things happen.
English shows the future with helper words like will, not by changing the verb's ending.
